calls.title: Michael / Kari
calls.summary: The meeting focused on refining the experiment creation process to enhance automation and clarity for users. Key enhancements included auto-selection of data sources to minimize manual steps, correcting SDK integration status in the checklist to reflect actual connections, and allowing analysis without SDK integration. Discussions on the pre-launch checklist clarified the distinction between hard and soft blockers, such as draft approval requirements. UI improvements were proposed to make the checklist less intrusive, including resizing, color adjustments, and better positioning. Additionally, the management of feature flag approvals was discussed to ensure checklist items remain visible and dynamic. Overall, the meeting emphasized improving user experience through better feedback and a simplified checklist design.
calls.keywords: sdk integration, experiment creation, pre-launch checklist, feature flag approval, UI design, data source selection
calls.action_items:
**Michael Samper**
Update checklist logic to mark SDK integration step as complete only when SDK connection is confirmed, not just when SDK exists in Growthbook (06:30)
Review code handling feature draft approvals to confirm if checklist item disappearing after approval is an engineering limitation; assess possibility to keep item visible or dynamically update approval status (15:40)

**Kari Kay**
Coordinate with Johnny to adjust text size and explore checklist height variations to improve UI usability, ensuring it adapts with min/max heights and does not obstruct page content (27:30)

calls.title: Michael / Kari
calls.summary: The team discussed several aspects of the interface, beginning with strict constraints on image sizes for variation cards to maintain proportions and eliminate awkward display issues. They agreed on a maximum width of 336 pixels and emphasized the need for proportional filling of image containers, allowing cropping while keeping full images accessible in lightbox views. The inconsistent modal systems for editing variations were also addressed, with proposals to consolidate them to improve user experience. Additionally, the distinction between buttons and link components was highlighted for clearer navigation, while challenges concerning the pre-launch checklist were reviewed, including usability in dark mode and managing displayed tasks. The overall goal is to design a cleaner interface capable of adapting to different user journeys.
calls.keywords: Image ratio, Variation edit modal, Prelaunch checklist, UI components, Traffic split, Experiment lifecycle
calls.action_items:

calls.title: Michael / Kari
calls.summary: The team engaged in refining the Visual Editor interface to enhance clarity and usability while addressing current design gaps and user workflows. Key updates included integrating URL targeting to provide full context for editors, rearranging edit controls for better user flow, and linking the URL header directly to launch the Visual Editor. Discussions also covered the lack of environment tracking and the need for follow-up enhancements. Although a major overhaul of the Visual Editor is needed, the team decided to focus on incremental improvements for the time being, while ensuring effective collaboration between product design and engineering to balance technical feasibility with user experience.
calls.keywords: Visual Editor, URL Targeting, Feature Flags, UI Design, Edit Button, Environment Data
calls.action_items:

**Kari Kay**

calls.title: Michael / Kari
calls.summary: The team discussed enhancements to the dialog component, concentrating on errors and the modal layout. Kari Kay presented a design pattern featuring error callouts and field highlights, while Michael Samper confirmed the handling of API errors with a custom component. They reviewed modal width and footer button consistency, deciding to standardize layouts and remove ambiguous close icons. The introduction of multi-step modals was proposed for handling complex workflows requiring revision selectors, differentiating single-feature edits from multi-feature scenarios. Discussions on evolving the design system highlighted the need for adaptable UI to minimize cognitive load, facilitating easier user navigation and decision-making.
calls.keywords: dialog component, modal design, error states, multi-step modal, feature flags, revision selector
